La verdad es que las partidas son bastante desafiantes para alguien nuevo que quiere integrarse al juego. Si logras superar esa barrera de frustración constante, la experiencia mejora, pero al principio es muy difícil. Ni siquiera puedes escoger un campeón que te guste para aprender a dominarlo, ya que al inicio casi siempre debes jugar con campeones aleatorios. Además, muchos jugadores suelen molestar o insultar a quienes aún no saben jugar, lo que hace la experiencia aún más frustrante. Para empeorar las cosas, el buscador de partidas rápidas puede tardar entre 4 y 7 minutos en encontrar una partida. El juego en sí es muy bueno, pero su curva de aprendizaje, junto con la imposibilidad de jugar desde el principio con el campeón que realmente te interesa, hacen que la experiencia inicial sea bastante mala.

Dota 2 is, without a doubt, one of the most frustrating games I’ve played in years. The main problem is its terrible balance: every patch seems to make things worse instead of better.
Far from improving the game, these constant updates end up making it repetitive and boring. What works today becomes useless tomorrow, forcing players to relearn everything from scratch over and over again. It’s not a natural evolution of the game—it’s an endless cycle that quickly becomes exhausting.
On top of that, the online experience is just as disappointing. The servers frequently have issues, crashes, or connection problems that ruin entire matches. There are times when you simply can’t play, either because of coordinator errors or matchmaking failures.
And as if that weren’t enough, the Steam platform doesn’t help either. Its servers are unstable and often become more of a problem than a support system. Slow downloads, disconnections, and technical issues make the overall experience even more frustrating.
In summary, Dota 2 is a poorly balanced game, with constant changes that make it tedious, and an online infrastructure that leaves a lot to be desired. An experience that could have been great, but ends up being more frustrating than enjoyable.
